A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SynFER, and their shared text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v2 includes Appendix A; v3 ends at the references despite directing readers to supplementary material for fine-tuning, implementation details and limitations. These unavailable counterparts limit parts of the comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation-quality evaluations, user-study outcomes, downstream recognition experiments, ablations, scaling results and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation-quality, recognition, ablation and scaling results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: The visible AU adapter, semantic guidance and FERAnno procedures match. However, v2 Section 4.2.2 specifies two-stage diffusion fine-tuning, whereas v3 replaces this description with a pointer to unavailable supplementary material. Whether the complete training procedure remains unchanged cannot be verified.

E1.justification: FEText sources and the documented supervised, self-supervised and compound-expression tasks match. v2 additionally details CAER-S fine-tuning and FERPlus zero-shot evaluation. v3 retains zero-shot claims and Figure 1 but lacks the corresponding detailed experiment; removal versus relocation cannot be established.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in the retained generation, self-supervised, supervised and few-shot tables. v2 Table 5 additionally compares FaRL, FLAVA, CLIP and Exp-CLIP variants, but its later counterpart is unavailable. EmojiDiff is newly discussed in related work, without a reported evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The added evaluation-metrics paragraph mainly explains existing procedures. Table 1 changes the MPS arrow from upward to downward while retaining the caption's above-1 preference convention, leaving the intended scoring direction unclear. Detailed settings in v2 Appendix A.2 also lack an accessible v3 counterpart.

E4.justification: The main component ablations and scaling analyses remain, while the FERAnno visualization drops the sadness example. v2 Appendix A.1 and A.3 additionally examine guidance-step sensitivity and over-smoothing. Their absence from the supplied v3 material prevents determining the full extent of analysis changes.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains the same reference to 95% confidence intervals while displaying point estimates without interval bounds. The supplied material provides no changed repeated-run counts, seed information, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds SynFER's MPS value of 0.50 in place of a dash. Tables 2–4, v2 Table 6/v3 Table 5 and the scaling curves otherwise match. Unavailable counterparts for the detailed zero-shot comparison and appendix results prevent reliably assessing the overall extent of result changes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical description of feature extraction and fusion remain unchanged. Neither version presents additional theorems, proofs or substantive derivations in the supplied material.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the assertion about existing methods' capabilities to categorical labels leveraging diffusion features and emphasizes SynFER as a synthesis pipeline. The central FEText, controllable generation and FERAnno contributions, together with the headline scaling claims, remain.

C2.justification: The main interpretations concerning synthetic-data benefits and distribution alignment are largely retained. v2 Appendix A.4 discusses slow generation, augmentation-only usage and restricted application scope; v3 directs readers to unavailable supplementary limitations. Retention or revision of these substantive qualifications cannot be established.

D1.justification: v2 promises future public code, whereas v3 states that code is available and supplies a repository link. However, v2's fine-tuning explanation and appendix details—including optimizer settings, training epochs, FAU mappings and guidance during the last five of 50 denoising steps—lack accessible later counterparts.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion newly positions SynFER against FineFace and newly cited EmojiDiff through downstream FER utility and label-semantic alignment. v3 also adds an FID reference and omits several citations associated with the unavailable zero-shot and implementation sections. The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the wording remain. v3 condenses selected passages, consolidates the contribution list, adds an evaluation-metrics paragraph and acknowledgments, updates authors and affiliations, and replaces the detailed fine-tuning subsection with a supplementary-material pointer.

P2.justification: The document undergoes substantial visual restructuring from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout, with redistributed tables and figures. FERAnno's schematic is redrawn compactly, and its attention visualization changes from three vertical examples to two horizontal examples. The scaling plots are reused and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies metric usage and research positioning and supplies a code-access link. However, its missing supplement prevents assessing retention of v2's reproducibility details, sensitivity evidence and limitations; the detailed zero-shot comparison is also unavailable. The unexplained MPS reporting revision adds ambiguity, preventing a reliable overall quality judgment.
